text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- The Serbian parliament holds an extraordinary session today to discuss draft amendments to the income tax law and law on social security contributions aimed at unburdening the economy.
- The repayment of Yugoslavia's foreign debt is both in its own interest and in that of its creditors, says member of the Yugoslav team in talks with the Paris and London Clubs Dragana Gnjatovic.
- Yugoslav and Bosnian expert teams started two-day talks in Belgrade Tuesday aimed at speeding up the establishment of economic ties which will centre on restoration of traffic communications.
- Slovenia warns about danger of Yugoslavia conducting separate talks on the succession issue following the meeting of central bank governors of the other four ex-Yugoslav republics in Skopje.
- Slovenian businessmen express great interest in Yugoslav markets at Celje handicrafts fair.

- "Slovenia remembers only its share of the foreign currency reserves of the former Yugoslavia but not what it owes," says Borka Vucic, director of the Beogradska Banka in Cyprus in response to a suit filed by Slovenia in Cyprus.
- Head of the Vojvodina provincial government Bosko Perosevic calls for full integration with the developed world at the inauguration of the agriculture fair in Novi Sad.
- Death plenalty to be replaced by life sentence in Yugoslavia's draft amendemnt of the criminal law, says president of the association for criminal law and criminology Ljubisa Lazarevic.
NASA BARBA
- Increasing number of workers of Kragujevac Zastava car manufacturer joining workers of Zastava arms in their one-month protest.
- Serbian Renewal Movement President Vuk Draskovic says Kragujevac workers are fighting for all Serbian workers.
- Milocer economists symposium on financial markets opens today.
- Yugoslav firms have difficulties in realizing the $330 million barter arrangement with China, so far deals worth only $70 million closed.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Partial election results in Bosnia show that members of the new Bosnian presidency will be Alija Izetbegovic, Kresimir Zubak and Momcilo Krajisnik, while the president of the Bosnian Serb Republic will be Biljana Plavsic.
- POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Central coordinating team for revival of Serbian economy says planned two-digit industrial output growth by end of year possible considering positive economic trends.
